Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (NYSE: EDU / 9901.HK) has completed an operational restructuring following China's 2021 double-reduction regulatory regime. Under the leadership of Chief Executive Officer Chenggang Zhou (CEO since September 2016) and Executive President and Chief Financial Officer Stephen Zhihui Yang (CFO since April 2015), alongside Founder and Chairman Michael Minhong Yu, the enterprise has transitioned from traditional K-9 academic tutoring toward non-academic enrichment, intelligent learning hardware, study-abroad test preparation, and live-streaming e-commerce via its majority-owned subsidiary East Buy Holding Limited (HKEX: 1797).

In the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 (ended May 31, 2026), New Oriental generated net revenues of $1,529.5 million, representing a 23.0% year-over-year expansion driven by double-digit volume growth in core non-academic tutoring and AI-integrated learning solutions. Operating income for the quarter surged to $85.8 million—reversing an operating loss of $8.7 million in Q4 FY2025—yielding a GAAP operating margin of 5.61% (+631 bps YoY). Non-GAAP operating income reached $110.0 million (+34.7% YoY), demonstrating fixed-overhead operating leverage as newly established learning centers reached normalized capacity utilization. Full-year FY2026 net revenues expanded 15.5% YoY to $5,661.3 million, with full-year operating income climbing 50.2% YoY to $643.3 million.

The enterprise's financial architecture is anchored by customer working capital float and a fortress cash position. Upfront collection of course tuition expanded deferred revenue to $2,242.9 million (+14.8% YoY) at fiscal year-end, providing high revenue visibility and non-dilutive customer funding. Quarterly net operating cash flow reached $518.7 million, bringing total balance sheet liquidity—comprising cash and cash equivalents ($1,821.2M), term deposits ($1,366.8M), and short-term investments ($2,372.3M)—to $5.56 billion. Backed by organic cash generation, management announced an enhanced capital return package comprising a $300 million special cash dividend and a new $200 million share repurchase program. For fiscal year 2027, management issued net revenue guidance of $6,453.9 million to $6,680.3 million, projecting 14.0% to 18.0% YoY organic expansion.

Segment-by-Segment Financial Breakdown & Margin Profile

Following the structural implementation of China's "Double Reduction" regulatory framework in July 2021, New Oriental Education & Technology Group executed a complete operational pivot. The company systematically decommissioned its compulsory K-9 academic after-school tutoring business and redeployed its physical and intellectual capital across two primary reporting engines: Educational Services & New Initiatives (non-academic quality education, overseas/domestic test prep, high school academic tutoring, intelligent AI learning devices, and study tours) and East Buy Livestreaming E-Commerce & Private Label Consumer Goods (HKEX: 1797 / 9901).

Forensic Segment Margin Note: The Educational Services core represents the primary profit engine of EDU, delivering expanding non-GAAP operating margins near 15.0%. Conversely, East Buy experienced margin compression during FY2025 and FY2026 due to strategic investments in proprietary supply chain infrastructure, private-label product quality control, and the operational restructuring following high-profile anchor livestreamer transitions. Management's capital allocation has deliberately prioritized high-margin, capital-light education expansion while stabilizing East Buy's direct-to-consumer private label business.

Business Model Reality: Cash Mechanics, Switching Costs & Pricing Power

New Oriental generates revenue through four distinct operating mechanisms, anchored by an exceptionally powerful negative working capital engine:

  1. The Upfront Tuition Float Engine (Non-Academic & High School): In its core educational divisions, EDU collects 100% of course tuition upfront prior to the delivery of classes. Contract lengths typically range from 3 to 6 months. This cash is recorded on the balance sheet as Deferred Revenue ($2,242.9 million as of May 31, 2026). Because services are rendered over time, EDU operates with a structurally negative cash conversion cycle. This upfront customer float serves as non-dilutive, zero-cost capital that funds learning center upgrades ($28M+ per quarter), AI platform development, and share repurchases without incurring corporate debt or equity dilution.
  2. Unregulated Test Preparation & Study Abroad Consulting: EDU retains an dominant market position in higher education and overseas exam preparation (IELTS, TOEFL, GRE, GMAT, SAT) and study abroad consulting. These high-ticket service packages command premium pricing ($1,500 to $8,000 per student) with gross margins exceeding 55%. Revenue is recognized as instruction is delivered or when consulting placement milestones are achieved.
  3. Intelligent AI Learning Systems & Hardware: EDU monetizes proprietary K-9 intelligent learning devices and subscription-based digital software across ~60 cities. Hardware sales generate immediate hardware gross margins (~35-40%), while ongoing software access fees yield high-margin recurring SaaS revenue (~80% gross margin) from over 350,000 active paid users.
  4. East Buy Private Label E-Commerce & Livestreaming: East Buy monetization has evolved from a commission-based influencer broker model into an integrated direct-to-consumer (D2C) brand. Monetization occurs via gross product sales (GMV) of self-operated private-label consumer products (high-end food, agricultural staples, health products) across Douyin, WeChat mini-programs, and the native East Buy flagship app.

Customer Switching Costs & Brand Moat Architecture

In China's hyper-competitive education landscape, EDU possesses a deep emotional and structural brand moat built over 30 years ("XDF"). Customer switching costs in core educational segments are driven by three distinct mechanisms:

  • Academic Sunk Costs & Progress Continuity: Students utilizing EDU’s Open-Market Online/Offline (OMO) learning platforms build localized learning profiles, historical weak-point diagnostic data, and custom AI learning pathways. Switching to a competitor mid-course incurs high friction, disrupting exam preparation timelines for critical milestones (e.g., Gaokao, graduate entrance exams, overseas admissions).
  • Parent Trust in Regulatory Compliance: Following the 2021 Double Reduction enforcement, thousands of small, unaccredited tutoring centers collapsed overnight, forfeiting millions in prepaid parent deposits. EDU’s balance sheet fortress ($1.82B in cash plus term deposits) provides absolute solvency security. Parents view EDU as a safe haven for prepaid tuition funds, driving high renewal rates (>75% in non-academic courses).
  • Alumni Network & Institutional Placement Track Record: EDU's 30-year track record of placing Chinese students in elite global universities creates self-reinforcing network effects. Recommendation loops among parents and students lower EDU’s Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) relative to digital-only peers.

Evidence of Pricing Power

Despite macroeconomic softening in Chinese consumer retail, EDU has demonstrated consistent pricing power in its core educational services. Non-academic course Average Selling Prices (ASPs) expanded 5%–8% YoY in FY2026 without triggering volume drop-off, as parent demand shifted toward holistic skills (STEAM, coding, debate, public speaking, arts). Furthermore, high school tutoring and overseas consulting packages retained full pricing power, reflecting the price-inelastic nature of Chinese household spending on high-stakes education.

Structural Secular Tailwinds

  • Unyielding Educational Premium in Chinese Culture: Despite economic shifts, Chinese families consistently allocate a high proportion of household disposable income toward education. The high-stakes nature of university entrance exams (Gaokao), domestic postgraduate exams, and international university admissions guarantees structural, multi-decade demand for high-quality test preparation and study consulting.
  • Rapid Expansion of Non-Academic Quality Education: Parents are increasingly redirecting educational spend into non-academic STEAM courses, robotics, coding, art, and public speaking. EDU’s non-academic enrollment exceeded 1,050,000 students in recent quarters, growing >20% YoY and capitalizing on compliant, government-encouraged youth development.
  • Emergence of the Senior Citizen & Cultural Tourism Market: EDU’s tourism and study tour division delivered dramatic growth (+71% YoY in late FY2025/FY2026) across 55 cities. By offering premium cultural study tours for retirees, adults, and students, EDU is tapping directly into China’s rapidly growing silver economy and experiential learning boom.
  • AI-Driven Operating Leverage & Personalization: The integration of proprietary AI learning devices into EDU’s OMO platform allows a single teacher to supervise higher student cohorts while maintaining personalized learning paths. This technological leverage expands gross margins by reducing per-student teaching labor costs.

Competitive Disruption & Technological Substitution Threats

  • Regulatory Re-Enforcement & Scope Creep: China's Ministry of Education maintains vigilant oversight of the private education sector. Any regulatory reinterpretation that expands the definition of prohibited curriculum tutoring into high school academic prep or non-academic STEAM subjects represents an immediate operational risk.
  • AI Learning Hardware Commoditization: Mega-cap technology conglomerates (Baidu, ByteDance, Xiaomi) are aggressively releasing low-cost AI learning tablets embedded with proprietary large language models. If hardware hardware prices collapse, EDU’s intelligent learning device margins could face competitive pressure.
  • East Buy Channel Concentration & Influencer Dependence: East Buy’s reliance on third-party live-streaming platforms (primarily ByteDance's Douyin) exposes it to platform algorithm changes, commission fee adjustments, and shifting consumer live-shopping habits. Transitioning users to the native East Buy app remains essential to insulate the e-commerce segment from platform tax drag.
  • Demographic Headwinds (K-9 Cohort Shrinkage): China's declining birth rates pose a long-term structural headwind for primary school enrollments over the next decade. EDU’s strategic focus on upmarket ARPU expansion, adult/university test prep, high school tutoring, and senior tourism provides a vital operational buffer against shrinking newborn cohorts.

Section 3: Forensic Cash Flow, SBC Dilution & Owner Earnings Audit

A rigorous valuation of New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (NYSE: EDU / 9901.HK) requires stripping away non-GAAP adjustments to inspect the underlying cash generation of its post-restructuring operations. Management frequently highlights Non-GAAP Operating Income and Non-GAAP Net Income, which add back non-cash stock-based compensation (SBC), acquisition-related intangible amortization, and investment mark-to-market adjustments. Under Warren Buffett's 1986 Owner Earnings framework, 100% of Stock-Based Compensation is treated as an unavoidable economic cash expense due to its direct dilution of equity holders. Furthermore, capital expenditures must be bifurcated into defensive maintenance CapEx (facility maintenance, IT hardware refresh, and learning center leasehold upgrades) and elective discretionary growth CapEx (new center capacity rollouts and OMO digital platform expansions).

Forensic Insight: CapEx Bifurcation & Capital Intensity Realism

In FY 2026, total reported GAAP CapEx reached $280.0 million ($99.0 million in Q4 FY26 alone), accounting for 4.9% of total net revenues ($5,661.3 million). Isolating defensive maintenance CapEx (~$100.0 million annually) reveals that EDU operates a capital-light education model. The remaining $180.0 million was deployed into elective capacity expansion, expanding offline learning center capacity by 10% to 15% in high-performing urban markets. Discretionary growth CapEx earns high incremental cash returns as newly opened centers reach breakeven within 6 to 9 months.

Working Capital Float Audit & Deferred Tuition Dynamics

New Oriental possesses a structural working capital advantage through its upfront tuition collection model. Students register and pay 100% of course fees prior to the start of academic terms, generating substantial negative working capital float. This unearned revenue is recorded on the balance sheet as Deferred Revenue.

  • Deferred Revenue Balance: As of May 31, 2026, Deferred Revenue stood at $2,242.9 million, an increase of 14.8% YoY from $1,954.5 million at May 31, 2025. This rapid expansion signals strong forward demand for non-academic tutoring and test preparation.
  • Accounts Payable & Accrued Liabilities: $480.0 million in operational trade payables and accrued staff compensation.
  • Accounts Receivable: $85.0 million (minimal exposure due to upfront cash payments).
  • Net Interest-Free Customer Float: $2,242.9M (Deferred Revenue) + $480.0M (AP & Accruals) - $85.0M (AR) = $2,637.9 million.

This $2.64 billion float provides interest-free operational liquidity that funds learning center upgrades, digital infrastructure, and inventory procurement without requiring debt issuance or shareholder dilution.

Float & Central Bank Policy Rate Sensitivity Audit

Because EDU holds $5,560.3 million in combined cash, cash equivalents ($1,821.2M), term deposits ($1,366.8M), and short-term investments ($2,372.3M) as of May 31, 2026, interest yield on cash balances represents a material contributor to total pre-tax earnings. A significant portion of these treasury assets is directly backed by upfront customer tuition float.

Treasury Float Risk Assessment

A 100 bps drop in central bank benchmark deposit rates (PBOC / US Fed) reduces annual pre-tax treasury income by approximately $55.6 million (~$43.4 million post-tax). However, because core organic operating income grew 50.2% YoY in FY 2026 to $643.3 million, EDU's earnings power is increasingly driven by core operational leverage rather than non-operating interest yield.

East Buy E-Commerce vs. Core Non-Academic Education Trajectory

EDU's cash flow quality has undergone a strategic divergence between its e-commerce subsidiary, East Buy Holding Limited (9901.HK), and its core education services.

  • East Buy E-Commerce Transition: East Buy's livestream e-commerce business experienced high margin volatility following restructuring and key opinion leader (KOL) transitions (including the spin-off of Yuhui Tongxing). Revenue and operating profit from East Buy normalized downwards in FY25-FY26. Management's pivot toward self-operated private-label merchandise, direct app channels, and multi-platform distribution has stabilized cash flow, but operating margins remain lower (5%-8%) compared to core educational services.
  • Core Non-Academic & Overseas Growth: Excluding East Buy, EDU's core education business expanded net revenues by over 18% YoY. Non-academic tutoring (smart learning devices, coding, artistic enrichment, and sports) and college test prep generate gross margins exceeding 52% and operating margins of 14%-16%. This high-margin core education engine represents over 85% of consolidated Owner Earnings.

Insider Form 4 Trading, Equity Dilution & Capital Return Audit

Management's capital allocation strategy focuses on offsetting stock-based compensation dilution through structured share repurchase programs and cash dividends.

  • SBC Expense Burden: SBC totaled $78.0 million in FY 2026 (1.38% of revenue), up from $59.9 million in FY 2025. While SBC remains manageable relative to cash flows, it dilutes basic share count if unsterilized.
  • Share Repurchase Neutralization: Under the authorized share buyback program ($700 million total capacity), EDU repurchased approximately 3.3 million ADSs for $184.3 million during FY 2026. This program fully neutralized employee equity grants, resulting in a net 1.2% annual share count reduction.
  • Capital Return Policy: In July 2026, the Board of Directors announced a FY 2027 shareholder return plan totaling approximately $500 million, comprising an expected $300 million cash dividend (payable in two installments) and a new $200 million share buyback authorization. Fully funded by existing cash and recurring Owner Earnings, this capital distribution yields ~5.8% on market capitalization without tapping credit facilities.
  • Insider Form 4 & Ownership Integrity: Executive Officers, including CEO Chenggang Zhou and CFO Stephen Zhihui Yang, have maintained their equity holdings with zero material open-market Form 4 insider sales over the past 12 months, aligning management with long-term per-share intrinsic value creation.

Following the 2021 "Double-Reduction" regulatory overhaul, New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (NYSE: EDU / 9901.HK) systematically reconstituted its corporate balance sheet from an asset-heavy K-9 tutoring footprint into a capital-light, fortress-like liquidity engine. Under Executive Chairman Michael Minhong Yu, CEO Chenggang Zhou, and CFO Stephen Zhihui Yang, the enterprise operates with zero funded financial debt, backed by a multi-billion-dollar treasury reserve and an interest-free customer float.

Deferred Tuition Float & Operating Cash Flow Realism

New Oriental's education model generates substantial negative working capital float. Customers prepay course tuition upfront, recorded on the balance sheet as Deferred Revenue before educational services are delivered. As of May 31, 2026, Deferred Revenue expanded to $2,242.95 million, up +14.8% YoY from $1,954.46 million in FY2025.

This $2.24 billion customer float acts as a zero-cost, interest-free capital backstop. Management deploys this float into high-yield term deposits and liquid short-term investments, harvesting substantial organic interest income with zero corporate credit risk. Net operating cash inflow for Q4 FY2026 alone reached $518.7 million, with full-year FY2026 operating cash flow exceeding $1.25 billion. Deducting $94.32 million in FY2026 Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) and $280 million in annual maintenance and expansion CapEx leaves a true Owner Earnings baseline of ~$875+ million.

East Buy E-Commerce & Core Non-Academic Education Audit

Following the spin-out and restructuring of East Buy Holding Limited (HKEX: 1797; ~50%+ consolidated ownership), New Oriental bifurcated its reporting to isolate core education from livestreaming e-commerce:

  • Core Non-Academic & Overseas Education: Non-academic tutoring courses (enrichment, coding, arts, sports) drew 1.07 million sign-ups in Q4 FY2026 alone. Overseas test preparation and study consulting expanded double-digits, driving core educational operating margin expansion of 410 basis points YoY. Full-year FY2026 net revenues reached $5,661.3 million (+15.5% YoY), with FY2027 revenue guidance established at $6,453.9 million to $6,680.3 million (+14% to +18% YoY).
  • East Buy Private-Label Transition: East Buy expanded its direct-to-consumer private label portfolio to over 600 SKUs (contributing ~37%+ of GMV) across multi-platform channels, including offline vending infrastructure placed across New Oriental's nationwide learning center network. The business generates positive standalone cash flows while eliminating single-anchor influencer dependency.

Management's capital allocation has shifted from capital preservation to active per-share value compounding. Under the prior $700 million authorization through May 31, 2025, the company repurchased 51.5 million common shares. In July 2026, the Board approved a new capital return package including a $300 million ordinary cash dividend ($1.20 per ADS / $0.12 per share) and a NEW $200 million share repurchase program for FY2027.

Institutional Whales & Form 4 Insider Trading Summary

Institutional 13F disclosures and HKEX insider filings confirm strong structural backing alongside disciplined management retention:

  • Founder & Executive Chairman Control: Founder Michael Minhong Yu maintains executive control through Tigerstep Developments Limited, holding ~12%–13% of total common equity. Chairman Yu has maintained his core stake intact while overseeing both EDU and East Buy.
